stem: In the figure shown, \(ABCD\) is a square, point \(E\) lies on \(\overline{AB}\), and point \(F\) lies on \(\overline{BC}\). What is the area of triangle \(DEF\)?
solution: The square has side \(4 + 6 = 10\), so its area is \(100\).
Subtract the three right triangles in the corners: \(\frac{1}{2}(10)(4) = 20\) at \(A\), \(\frac{1}{2}(6)(6) = 18\) at \(B\), and \(\frac{1}{2}(4)(10) = 20\) at \(C\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is \(20 + 18 + 20\), the total area of the three corner triangles, not triangle \(DEF\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is half the square's area; a triangle with a vertex at \(D\) has half the square's area only when its base is a full side of the square.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is \(100 - 20 - 18\); it leaves out the corner triangle \(FCD\).

verify:
choices = {o: choices[n] for o, n in {'C': 'A', 'B': 'B', 'A': 'C', 'D': 'D'}.items()}; answer = {'A': 'C', 'B': 'B', 'C': 'A', 'D': 'D'}[answer]  # shuffled: original letters
P=figure['points']
o=['D','E','F']
ans=Rational(1,2)*abs(sum(P[o[i]][0]*P[o[(i+1)%3]][1]-P[o[(i+1)%3]][0]*P[o[i]][1] for i in range(3)))
assert P['E'][0]-P['A'][0]==4 and P['B'][0]-P['E'][0]==6 and P['F'][1]-P['B'][1]==6 and P['C'][1]-P['F'][1]==4
assert ans==100-20-18-20==42
assert value(choices[answer])==ans
assert all(value(choices[k])!=ans for k in choices if k!=answer)
assert value(choices['C'])==20+18+20 and value(choices['D'])==100-20-18
